value_domain: ABS Address Register identifier (hashed and truncated)
value_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
variable_description: The apprentice's address, for one period bounded by START_DATE and END_DATE. The mesh block, SA1, SA2, SA4 and state columns beside it are that address geocoded, and ICP_MB flags an Indigenous community mesh block. Because apprenticeships are commonly served away from home, the address history here is what separates a change of residence from a change of employer.
value_definition: A hash of the address register identifier, truncated. The ABS Address Register is the ABS's list of every known physical address in Australia, built from Geoscape's Geocoded National Address File and extended with each address's use and its dwelling structure. Hashing replaces the identifier with a code carrying none of the address, so the value has no internal structure and cannot be decoded. There is no finite list to publish.
limitation: The identifier stands for an address, not for a person or a household, so a shared value shows co-residence rather than a relationship. The address is the one the apprenticeship system held, which for an apprentice living away for training can be a family address rather than a current residence. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions, so a shared value is strong evidence of a shared address rather than proof of one.
rationale: The DIL gives the field as a hashed ARID on the apprentice address table, which carries start and end dates, the ASGS codes and the person identifier. ABS publishes what the Address Register identifier is.
evidence_quote: an up-to-date, comprehensive list of all known physical addresses within Australia
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Hashed arid' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_source: ABS, Creating a child mobility indicator using the Life Course Dataset
variable_description: The address a person lived at, held as a key rather than as text. In plida_core_loc and the per-source address tables one row is one episode: the person was at this address from START_DATE to END_DATE, and the MB, SA1, SA2 and SA4 columns beside it are that address geocoded. The ar_addr table is the other side of the join, holding one row per address with its use and its dwelling structure, so the identifier is what turns a location episode into a described dwelling. Because the key is the address and not the person, everyone living there carries the same value, and SOURCE_FLAG records which agency's records the episode was drawn from.
description_source: ABS, Creating a child mobility indicator using the Life Course Dataset
value_definition: A hash of the address register identifier, truncated. The ABS Address Register is the ABS's list of every known physical address in Australia, built from Geoscape's Geocoded National Address File and extended with each address's use and its dwelling structure. Hashing replaces the identifier with a code carrying none of the address, so the value has no internal structure and cannot be decoded. There is no finite list to publish.
limitation: The identifier stands for an address, not for a person, a household or a dwelling, so a shared value shows co-residence rather than a relationship. An administrative address is only as current as the person's last dealing with the agency, so an episode can outlast a move. ABS found that 4.3% to 11.2% of children with an address history between 2006 and 2021 were missing an ARID, and the version of Core Locations used for the child mobility indicator imputes those gaps. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions, so a shared value is strong evidence of a shared address rather than proof of one.
rationale: The PLIDA DIL names the field Address Register ID. ABS documents the Core Locations module as holding a secure hashed ARID standing for each address in the ABS Address Register, and describes the address history structure (ARID with start and end dates of residence) that the registry's own table layout shows: SPINE_ID, ARID, START_DATE, END_DATE and the ASGS codings, with ar_addr holding address use and dwelling structure against the same key.
evidence_quote: a secure hashed Address Register Identifier (ARID) that represents each address in the ABS Address Register
supersedes_rationale: The domain was marked guessed with the generic sentence 'The domain is open, so no finite value list applies.' ABS publishes what the identifier is and how it is de-identified, which makes the domain sourced and lets the entry say what the column is for.

value_definition: A hash of the address register identifier, truncated. variable_description: The address derived for an income support recipient, for one period bounded by START_DATE and END_DATE. Centrelink holds several addresses for a customer at once, so ADDR_PRTY ranks them and ADR_TYP separates a residence from a postal address; the identifier is the derived winner rather than a raw field. CMTY_CODE marks a discrete community address and CNTRY_CDE carries the country where the address is overseas.
value_definition: A hash of the address register identifier, truncated. The ABS Address Register is the ABS's list of every known physical address in Australia, built from Geoscape's Geocoded National Address File and extended with each address's use and its dwelling structure. Hashing replaces the identifier with a code carrying none of the address, so the value has no internal structure and cannot be decoded. There is no finite list to publish.
limitation: The identifier stands for an address, not for a person or a household, so a shared value shows co-residence rather than a relationship. Income support obliges recipients to keep an address current, which makes this source more responsive to a move than most, but a nominee or care arrangement can put a recipient's address somewhere they do not live. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions, so a shared value is strong evidence of a shared address rather than proof of one.
rationale: The PLIDA DIL gives the field as a hashed, truncated ARID on the DOMINO derived location table, which carries an address priority, an address type and start and end dates. ABS publishes what the Address Register identifier is.

value_domain: ABS Address Register identifier (hashed and truncated)
value_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
variable_description: The address held on the person's Medicare enrolment, for one period of their address history bounded by START_DATE and END_DATE. Medicare addresses update when a person deals with the system, which for children and for anyone with regular claims is often, so this is one of the more current address sources feeding Core Locations. ADR_TYP separates a residential address from a postal one and CNTRY_CDE carries the country where the address is overseas.
value_definition: A hash of the address register identifier, truncated. The ABS Address Register is the ABS's list of every known physical address in Australia, built from Geoscape's Geocoded National Address File and extended with each address's use and its dwelling structure. Hashing replaces the identifier with a code carrying none of the address, so the value has no internal structure and cannot be decoded. There is no finite list to publish.
limitation: The identifier stands for an address, not for a person or a household, so a shared value shows co-residence rather than a relationship. A Medicare address belongs to the enrolment, so children on a parent's card carry that parent's address whether or not they live there. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions, so a shared value is strong evidence of a shared address rather than proof of one.
rationale: The PLIDA DIL gives the field as a hashed address register id on the Medicare enrolments address tables, whose start and end dates bound the episode. ABS publishes what the Address Register identifier is, and documents Core Locations as combining source address histories of this shape.
evidence_quote: an up-to-date, comprehensive list of all known physical addresses within Australia
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'not specified' as its domain and the same generic sentence as both its value definition and its limitation.

value_domain: ABS Address Register identifier (hashed and truncated)
value_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
variable_description: The address the ATO held for the individual on the income tax return context and payment summary records. It is the key behind the ASGS geography on the same row, and the key that matches the individual's address here to the same address in Core Locations and in the other ATO products, so a residence can be followed across returns without any address text.
value_definition: A hash of the address register identifier, truncated. The ABS Address Register is the ABS's list of every known physical address in Australia, built from Geoscape's Geocoded National Address File and extended with each address's use and its dwelling structure. Hashing replaces the identifier with a code carrying none of the address, so the value has no internal structure and cannot be decoded. There is no finite list to publish.
limitation: The identifier stands for an address, not for a person or a household, so a shared value shows co-residence rather than a relationship. An administrative address is only as current as the taxpayer's last dealing with the ATO, so it can lag a move by a year or more. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions, so a shared value is strong evidence of a shared address rather than proof of one.
rationale: The PLIDA DIL gives the field as a hashed, truncated ARID, and ABS publishes what the Address Register and its identifier are.
evidence_quote: an up-to-date, comprehensive list of all known physical addresses within Australia

value_domain: ABS Address Register identifier (hashed and truncated)
value_source: ABS Address Register Information Guide
variable_description: The rental property's address, not the landlord's. Every amount on the row belongs to this property: rent received, loan interest, council rates, repairs, agent fees. That makes the identifier the thing that turns a taxpayer-year file into a property-year one, because a property held jointly appears once per owner, each with their own OWNRSHP_PRCNT, all carrying the same value. It also follows the property across years and across changes of owner.
value_definition: A hash of the address register identifier, truncated. The ABS Address Register is the ABS's list of every known physical address in Australia, built from Geoscape's Geocoded National Address File and extended with each address's use and its dwelling structure. Hashing replaces the identifier with a code carrying none of the address, so the value has no internal structure and cannot be decoded. There is no finite list to publish.
limitation: The identifier stands for the address, not for the property title or the tenancy, and it says nothing about who lived there. A landlord's own residence can appear here too, since a taxpayer with more than one rental property files a row for each. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions, so a shared value is strong evidence of the same property rather than proof of it.
rationale: The rental property schedule reports income and expenses per property, and the identifier sits with GEOCODED_INDEX, LGA_CODE_2024 and MB_CODE_2021 on the same row as the rent, interest and expense amounts, which are property-level quantities. The ATO's schedule collects the property address, so the geocoded address on the row is the property's.
evidence_quote: an up-to-date, comprehensive list of all known physical addresses within Australia
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'not specified' as its domain and the same generic sentence twice, hiding the most useful fact about the file, which is that it can be analysed by property.
